newsitem.title: GERMANY: VWgets larger share of global market.
newsitem.headline: VWgets larger share of global market.

text.p: Volkswagen AG, profiting from a gamble on international sales, said Tuesday its global deliveries rose to nearly 4 million vehicles in 1996, making the German carmaker the fourth largest in the world.

VW said worldwide vehicle deliveries rose to 3.966 million units in 1996 compared with 3.560 million in 1995, giving it 10 percent of the global passenger vehicle market in 1996 compared with 9.4 percent a year earlier.
The gains were impressive in the weak European market, where VW reported vehicle deliveries excluding Germany of 1.39 million vehicles, a gain of 14.7 percent for the year.

Prospects for higher 1997 sales, as well as an increase in market share, will be pinned on the launch of the new Golf as well as other new products, including a mini-car dubbed the VW Lupino and intensive marketing efforts, VW officials said.

But the higher foreign sales, which included a 41 percent gain in eastern Europe, were dampened by a meagre 2.6 percent increase in domestic sales to 969,400 vehicles at a time when Germany's total vehicle sales rose about 5 percent.
The lackluster performance in Germany lost VW some of its domestic market share, which slipped to 19 percent from 19.4 percent in 1995.

But it was still ahead of Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors Corp., at 16 percent, with which it ended in early January a bitter four-year-old feud over charges of industrial spying when it lured away production guru Jose Ignacio Lopez.
